title: LLMs as Research Tools: A Large Scale Survey of Researchers’ Usage and Perceptions

bias_targets.methodology: Large-scale survey and linear mixed-effects modeling comparing LLM usage frequency, perceived benefits, and ethical concerns between White and Non-White researchers.
Large-scale survey and linear mixed-effects modeling evaluating differences in perceived ethics, risks, and usage of LLMs between men, women, and non-binary researchers.

Analyzing survey responses using statistical models to measure differences in LLM usage (particularly for editing tasks) and perceived equity benefits between native and non-native English-speaking researchers.
Comparing survey ratings across researchers of different career stages (junior vs. senior) to evaluate disparities in perceived benefits and ethical concerns regarding LLM usage.
Qualitative thematic analysis of open-ended, free-text survey responses to identify researchers' concerns about LLM outputs containing biases, marginalization, and stereotypes.
